catalog.name: Units of Measure and Packaging calculations
catalog.description: Every formula, algorithm, rounding rule and worked example of the units of measure and packaging domain, in a structured form a rebuild can test against: the precision step and the rounding function with its five methods, its floating-point compensation term, its tie-repaired whole-number rounding and its accurate inversion of a step; the per-unit rounding, the comparison, the zero test and the euclidean division at a precision; the derivation of an absolute quantity from a contained quantity, the length chain that is not exactly representable, the inversion of that derivation, the delivered unit table with its derived absolute quantities and sequences, and the quantity ladder of the counting tree; the quantity conversion algorithm with its four short-circuits, its cross-tree behaviour and its round-trip drift; the complete conversion matrix of the counting, mass, volume, working time, length and surface trees in both directions under three rounding methods; the six mandatory worked examples; the shared-ancestor test; the price conversion, the price list rule formula and the quantity that matches a rule; the whole-packaging rounding, its packaging quantity and the full-packaging reservation; the unit propagation parameter in both settings, the reservation double conversion, the serial-tracked reduction and the relabelling that follows a change of a product's own unit; every crossing of the master table of document boundaries, from vendor selection to the storefront cart; the sequence and the rounding precision of a unit, the discounted vendor price, the purchase line total quantity and gross unit price, the packaging quantity on a move, the bulk weight, the package weight, the shipping weight and volume, the content description of a package, the kit and production component quantities, the two unbuild ratios and the catalogue aggregated quantity; the rounding edges, from conversions that round to zero and conversions that inflate to precisions of zero and of more than two digits, the comparison-versus-difference trap, negative quantities and the three contained-quantity pathologies; the effects of changing the global precision and the off-grid refusal; and the financial boundary, with the extended amount of a line, the price scaled to the line's unit, the delivered quantity derived from analytic lines, the two accrual variants and the audit of a suspected unit-related ledger error.

records.name: The rounding step derived from a number of precision digits
records.purpose: Turns the digit count held by the `Product Unit` decimal precision record into the step that every quantity of the domain is snapped onto, so that a rebuild can express a precision either way and obtain the same grid.

operands.name: precision digits
operands.unit_or_currency: a count of decimal digits, no unit
operands.source: the number of digits of the `Product Unit` decimal precision record, whose shipped value is two
operands.constraints: a whole number greater than or equal to zero

preconditions.condition: Exactly one of the two forms is supplied: a number of digits or a step.
preconditions.otherwise: Supplying both, or neither, is a programming error and must fail loudly.

preconditions.condition: A step supplied directly is strictly greater than zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The assertion fails and the rounding function refuses the call.

procedure: Read the number of digits of the `Product Unit` decimal precision record.
Raise ten to the power of the negated digit count.
Use the resulting step wherever a rounding grid is needed; every unit reports this same step as its rounding precision.
records.formula: step = 10 ^ ( − precision_digits )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the operation produces the step that other operations round onto.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.method: None.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

records.name: The rounding function, normalise, apply and denormalise
records.purpose: The single function every quantity of the platform passes through. It converts a value into whole steps, applies the chosen method there, and converts back, so that all rounding in the domain is one reproducible operation.

operands.name: value
operands.unit_or_currency: the quantity being rounded, in whatever unit or currency the caller holds
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: a real number; negative values are permitted

operands.name: precision
operands.unit_or_currency: either a count of decimal digits or a step expressed as a fraction of one
operands.source: the caller, in practice the `Product Unit` decimal precision record or a literal step of one
operands.constraints: exactly one of the two forms, the step strictly positive, the digit count a whole number greater than or equal to zero

operands.name: rounding method
operands.unit_or_currency: one of five named methods, no unit
operands.source: the caller; the function's own default is half away from zero
operands.constraints: one of half away from zero, half towards zero, half to even, away from zero, towards zero

preconditions.condition: Exactly one of the digit count and the step is supplied.
preconditions.otherwise: The call fails loudly as a programming error.

preconditions.condition: The named rounding method is one of the five.
preconditions.otherwise: The call fails with a message naming the unknown method.

procedure: Resolve the step: use the supplied step, or ten raised to minus the supplied digit count.
If the step is zero, or the value is zero, return zero immediately.

Choose the scaling direction: normalising divides by the step and denormalising multiplies by it, but when the step is smaller than one, replace the step by its accurately inverted value and swap the two operations so that normalising multiplies by the large whole number and denormalising divides by it.
Normalise the value, obtaining the value expressed in whole steps plus a fraction.
Compute the compensation term from the magnitude of the normalised value.
Apply the chosen method to the normalised value, obtaining a whole number.
Denormalise the whole number and return it.
records.formula: rounded_value = denormalize( apply_method( normalize( value ) ) )

rounding.what: The normalised value, that is the value expressed in whole steps.
rounding.precision: One step, where the step is ten raised to minus the precision digits, or the step supplied directly.
rounding.method: The method named by the caller; the function's own default is half away from zero.
rounding.step: After normalising and before denormalising; the value is never rounded in its original scale.

result.name: rounded value
result.unit_or_currency: the same unit or currency as the value
result.stored_or_displayed: returned to the caller, which stores or displays it

edge_cases.case: The value is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Zero is returned by the short-circuit, with no method applied.

edge_cases.case: The step is smaller than one, which is the ordinary case.
edge_cases.outcome: The step is inverted accurately and the two scaling operations are swapped, so that a division by a small fraction never occurs.

edge_cases.case: The value is negative zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign is carried through the whole-number step, so negative zero is returned rather than positive zero.

edge_cases.case: The step is a value the inversion table does not hold.
edge_cases.outcome: The inverse is computed from the scientific rendering of the step; see the accurate inversion record.

records.name: The rounding function applied half away from zero
records.purpose: The method the rounding function itself defaults to, and the method used at every boundary where the result is a physical quantity that will be compared with or subtracted from a quantity on hand.

operands.name: normalised value
operands.unit_or_currency: the value expressed in whole steps plus a fraction, no unit
operands.source: step four of the rounding function

operands.name: compensation term
operands.unit_or_currency: a dimensionless correction, no unit

preconditions.condition: The value has already been normalised onto whole steps.

records.name: The rounding function applied half to even
records.purpose: The method that resolves a tie to the nearer even multiple of the step, offered by the rounding function and selectable wherever a rounding method is a parameter.

operands.name: normalised value
operands.unit_or_currency: the value expressed in whole steps plus a fraction, no unit
operands.source: step four of the rounding function

operands.name: compensation term
operands.unit_or_currency: a dimensionless correction, no unit
operands.source: two raised to the power of the base-two logarithm of the absolute normalised value minus fifty

preconditions.condition: The value has already been normalised onto whole steps.
preconditions.otherwise: The tie test would be taken against the whole numbers rather than against the step grid.

procedure: Take the whole part below the normalised value, that is its floor.
Take the absolute difference between the normalised value and that floor.
If that difference is within the compensation term of one half, the value is a tie: return the floor plus one when the floor is odd, and the floor itself when the floor is even.
Otherwise round the normalised value half away from zero to a whole number.
Denormalise and return.
records.formula: difference = | normalized_value − floor( normalized_value ) | ; tie when | difference − 0.5 | ≤ epsilon ; rounded_whole = floor + 1 when floor is odd , floor when floor is even ; otherwise rounded_whole = round_half_away_from_zero_to_whole( normalized_value )

rounding.precision: One step of the resolved precision.
rounding.method: Half to even: the nearest step, and a value exactly halfway goes to the nearer even multiple of the step.
rounding.step: On the normalised value, before denormalising.

result.name: rounded value
result.unit_or_currency: the same unit or currency as the value
result.stored_or_displayed: returned to the caller

edge_cases.case: The floor is negative and odd, for example minus three.
edge_cases.outcome: The floor plus one is minus two, which is the nearer even whole number, so the method remains symmetric about zero in the sense that it always moves to an even multiple.

edge_cases.case: The value is not a tie but lies within the compensation term of one half because of accumulated floating-point error.
edge_cases.outcome: It is treated as a tie; this is the deliberate purpose of using fifty rather than fifty-two in the compensation term.

worked_examples.description: One half at zero digits
worked_examples.narrative: The floor is zero, which is even, so the tie resolves to zero.

worked_examples.description: One and one half at zero digits
worked_examples.narrative: The floor is one, which is odd, so the tie resolves to two.

worked_examples.description: Two and one half at zero digits
worked_examples.narrative: The floor is two, which is even, so the tie resolves to two; this is where half to even differs from half away from zero, which would give three.

records.purpose: The method that resolves a tie towards zero, offered by the rounding function and selectable wherever a rounding method is a parameter.

rounding.precision: One step of the resolved precision.
rounding.method: Half towards zero: the nearest step, and a value exactly halfway goes towards zero.
rounding.step: After the compensation term is subtracted and before denormalising.

edge_cases.outcome: The result moves towards zero, so minus one half at zero digits gives zero.

edge_cases.case: A value just above a tie by less than the compensation term.
edge_cases.outcome: The subtraction pulls it onto the tie and the tie is then resolved towards zero.

records.name: The rounding function applied away from zero
records.purpose: The default method of the quantity conversion operation, and the method used wherever the result is a commercial quantity that must not under-serve the counterparty.

operands.name: normalised value
operands.unit_or_currency: the value expressed in whole steps plus a fraction, no unit
operands.source: step four of the rounding function

operands.name: compensation term
operands.unit_or_currency: a dimensionless correction, no unit
operands.source: two raised to the power of the base-two logarithm of the absolute normalised value minus fifty

preconditions.condition: The value has already been normalised onto whole steps.
preconditions.otherwise: The added quantity of one minus the compensation term would push the value by one whole number instead of by one step.

procedure: Add to the normalised value, carrying the sign of the normalised value, the quantity one minus the compensation term.
Truncate the result towards zero to a whole number.
Denormalise and return.

rounding.precision: One step of the resolved precision.
rounding.method: Away from zero: any non-zero fractional part pushes the result to the next step further from zero.

edge_cases.case: A negative value.
edge_cases.outcome: It moves further negative, because the sign is carried on the added quantity.

records.name: The floating-point compensation term of the rounding function
records.purpose: Absorbs the representation error accumulated by the operations that produced the value, so that a value which is arithmetically a tie is recognised as a tie and a value which is arithmetically on a step is not pushed off it.

operands.name: normalised value
operands.unit_or_currency: the value expressed in whole steps plus a fraction, no unit
operands.source: step four of the rounding function
operands.constraints: not zero, because the function short-circuits on zero before this point

preconditions.condition: The normalised value is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The base-two logarithm is undefined; the zero short-circuit of the rounding function has already returned.

procedure: Take the absolute value of the normalised value.
Take its base-two logarithm, giving the magnitude.
Subtract fifty from the magnitude.
Raise two to that power; the result is the compensation term.
records.formula: epsilon = 2 ^ ( log2( | normalized_value | ) − 50 )

rounding.what: Nothing; the term is an addend used by the five methods.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.method: None.
rounding.step: Computed after normalising and before the method is applied.

result.name: compensation term
result.stored_or_displayed: used inside the rounding function only; never stored

edge_cases.case: A rebuild uses fifty-two, the minimal exponent that repairs a single unit in the last place.
edge_cases.outcome: Values such as two and six hundred seventy-five thousandths round differently, because the accumulated error of earlier operations is no longer absorbed.

edge_cases.case: A rebuild omits the term entirely.
edge_cases.outcome: Two and six hundred seventy-five thousandths rounds to two and sixty-seven hundredths instead of two and sixty-eight hundredths, and away-from-zero conversions push values that are arithmetically exact onto the next step.

edge_cases.case: The normalised value is very large.
edge_cases.outcome: The term scales with the magnitude, so it always represents the same relative error rather than the same absolute error.

worked_examples.description: The term at a normalised magnitude of about one hundred

expected_outputs.consequence: an excess smaller than about nine hundredths of a quadrillionth is absorbed

worked_examples.narrative: Two raised to the base-two logarithm of one hundred is one hundred, and dividing by two raised to the fiftieth gives roughly nine hundredths of a quadrillionth; this is why one and one quadrillionth rounds to one under the away-from-zero method at two digits.

worked_examples.description: The term at the tie of two and six hundred seventy-five thousandths
worked_examples.narrative: The normalised value sits a fraction below two hundred sixty-seven and one half; adding the term lifts it onto the tie, which then resolves away from zero to two hundred sixty-eight steps.

records.name: The nearest whole number half away from zero, with tie repair
records.purpose: The whole-number rounding used inside three of the five methods. It is deliberately not the round-half-to-even behaviour that language runtimes usually provide, and it detects and repairs a runtime tie.

operands.name: value
operands.unit_or_currency: the normalised value, no unit
operands.source: the method being applied inside the rounding function

preconditions.condition: The runtime offers a nearest-integer operation whose tie behaviour is known to be half to even.
preconditions.otherwise: The tie probe still works, because it only tests whether adding one increases the answer by exactly one.

procedure: Take the runtime's nearest-integer result for the value.
Take the runtime's nearest-integer result for the value plus one.
If the second result is not the first result plus exactly one, the value was a tie that the runtime resolved to the even side; return instead the value plus one half carrying the sign of the value.
Otherwise return the runtime's first result carrying the sign of the value.
The sign is carried so that rounding negative zero yields negative zero and so that the result is a real number rather than a whole number.
records.formula: probe = nearest_integer( value + 1 ) − nearest_integer( value ) ; result = sign( value ) × ( | value | + 0.5 ) when probe ≠ 1 , otherwise result = sign( value ) × nearest_integer( | value | )

rounding.what: The value, onto a whole number.
rounding.precision: One whole number.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, with the runtime's half-to-even tie detected and overridden.
rounding.step: Inside the method application of the rounding function, after the compensation term has been added or subtracted.

result.name: nearest whole number, ties away from zero
result.unit_or_currency: a whole number carried as a real number, no unit
result.stored_or_displayed: used inside the rounding function only

edge_cases.case: The value is negative zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Negative zero is returned, because the sign is carried.

edge_cases.case: The value is exactly halfway between two whole numbers.
edge_cases.outcome: The probe detects the runtime's even resolution and the result is pushed away from zero.

edge_cases.case: A rebuild uses the runtime's nearest-integer operation directly.
edge_cases.outcome: Ties resolve to even, and half-away-from-zero, half-towards-zero and away-from-zero rounding all diverge on tie values.

worked_examples.description: A positive tie
worked_examples.narrative: The probe is two rather than one, so the value was a tie resolved to even; the repaired result is the value plus one half, that is three.

worked_examples.description: A value that is not a tie
worked_examples.narrative: Adding one increases the runtime answer by exactly one, so the value was not a tie and the runtime result stands.

records.name: The accurate inversion of a rounding step
records.purpose: Turns a step smaller than one into the exact whole number that multiplying by it is equivalent to dividing by the step, so that normalising a value never divides by a small fraction and never introduces error of its own.

operands.name: step
operands.unit_or_currency: a fraction of one, no unit
operands.source: the resolved precision of the rounding function
operands.constraints: strictly greater than zero and smaller than one for the inversion to be applied

preconditions.condition: The step is strictly smaller than one.
preconditions.otherwise: No inversion is performed; normalising divides by the step and denormalising multiplies by it.

procedure: Look the step up in the table of exact inverses, which holds the thirty steps most commonly used: the tenths, hundredths, thousandths, ten-thousandths, hundred-thousandths, millionths, ten-millionths, hundred-millionths, billionths and ten-billionths, each in its one, two and five variants.

If the step is in the table, take its exact inverse: one tenth inverts to ten, two tenths to five, five tenths to two, one hundredth to one hundred, two hundredths to fifty, five hundredths to twenty, one thousandth to one thousand, two thousandths to five hundred, five thousandths to two hundred, one ten-thousandth to ten thousand, two ten-thousandths to five thousand, five ten-thousandths to two thousand, one hundred-thousandth to one hundred thousand, two hundred-thousandths to fifty thousand, five hundred-thousandths to twenty thousand, one millionth to one million, two millionths to five hundred thousand, five millionths to two hundred thousand, one ten-millionth to ten million, two ten-millionths to five million, five ten-millionths to two million, one hundred-millionth to one hundred million, two hundred-millionths to fifty million, five hundred-millionths to twenty million, one billionth to one billion, two billionths to five hundred million, five billionths to two hundred million, one ten-billionth to ten billion, two ten-billionths to five billion and five ten-billionths to two billion.
If the step is not in the table, render it in scientific notation with fifteen digits after the point, splitting it into a coefficient and an exponent.
Build the number whose coefficient is the same and whose exponent is negated.
Divide that number by the square of the coefficient and return the quotient.
records.formula: inverted_step = ( coefficient × 10 ^ ( − exponent ) ) ÷ coefficient²

rounding.what: Nothing; the operation produces an exact inverse.
rounding.precision: The scientific rendering uses fifteen digits after the point.
rounding.method: None.
rounding.step: Before normalising, whenever the step is smaller than one.

result.name: inverted step
result.unit_or_currency: a whole number of steps in one, no unit
result.stored_or_displayed: used inside the rounding function only

edge_cases.case: The step is exactly one.
edge_cases.outcome: No inversion; normalising divides by one and denormalising multiplies by one, both of which are exact.

edge_cases.case: The step is larger than one.
edge_cases.outcome: No inversion; the ordinary scaling direction is kept.

edge_cases.case: The step is a fraction that is not a power of ten, for example one eighth.
edge_cases.outcome: The general formula is used and returns the exact inverse.

records.name: Comparing two values in a unit
records.purpose: Decides whether one quantity is lower than, equal to or greater than another at the grid of the `Product Unit` precision. Every rule of the domain that says two quantities are equal means that this comparison returns zero.

operands.source: the caller

operands.name: second value
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the same unit
operands.source: the caller

operands.source: the `Product Unit` decimal precision record
operands.constraints: a whole number greater than or equal to zero

preconditions.condition: Both values are expressed in the same unit.
preconditions.otherwise: The comparison is meaningless; the caller must convert first.

procedure: If the two values are identical as stored, return zero immediately; the parameter checks still run but no rounding is performed.
Round each value onto the grid, half away from zero.
Take the difference of the two rounded values.
If that difference is zero at the same precision, return zero.
Otherwise return minus one when the difference is negative and plus one when it is positive.

rounding.precision: The `Product Unit` precision, one hundredth as shipped.

records.name: Testing a value for zero in a unit
records.purpose: Decides whether a quantity counts as nothing at the grid of the `Product Unit` precision. Every rule of the domain that says a quantity is zero means that this test returns true.

operands.name: value
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the unit the operation is invoked on
operands.source: the caller

operands.name: step
operands.unit_or_currency: a fraction of one unit, no currency
operands.source: the rounding precision of the unit, which is the `Product Unit` step

preconditions.condition: The value is expressed in the unit whose step is used.
preconditions.otherwise: A quantity that is nothing in one unit may be substantial in another; the caller must convert first.

procedure: Return true when the value is exactly zero.
Otherwise round the value onto the grid half away from zero.
Take the absolute value of the rounded result.
Return true when that absolute value is strictly smaller than the step, and false otherwise.
records.formula: is_zero = ( value = 0 ) or ( | round_to_precision( value , step ) | < step )

rounding.what: The value, before the magnitude test.
rounding.precision: The `Product Unit` step, one hundredth as shipped.
rounding.method: Half away from zero.
rounding.step: After any subtraction the caller performed, which is what distinguishes the zero test from the comparison.

result.name: is zero
result.stored_or_displayed: returned to the caller and used by guards throughout the platform

edge_cases.case: A value of four thousandths at two digits.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds to zero, whose absolute value is smaller than one hundredth, so the test returns true.

edge_cases.case: A value of six thousandths at two digits.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds to one hundredth, which is not smaller than one hundredth, so the test returns false.

edge_cases.case: A negative value just above minus one step.
edge_cases.outcome: The absolute value is taken after rounding, so the test is symmetric about zero.

worked_examples.description: The difference of the canonical divergence pair
worked_examples.narrative: Six thousandths minus two thousandths is four thousandths, which rounds to zero and therefore tests as zero, while the same two values compare as different.

worked_examples.description: A value that is not zero at the grid
worked_examples.narrative: Six thousandths rounds up to one hundredth, which is not smaller than the step, so the value is not zero.

records.name: Euclidean division at a precision
records.purpose: Splits a quantity into a whole number of packs and a leftover, both free of representation error, wherever a quantity must be expressed as whole multiples plus a remainder.

operands.name: dividend
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in a unit of measure
operands.source: the caller

operands.name: divisor
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the same unit
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: a real number other than zero

operands.name: precision
operands.unit_or_currency: either a count of decimal digits or a step
operands.source: the caller, in practice the `Product Unit` precision
operands.constraints: exactly one of the two forms, the step strictly positive

preconditions.condition: Exactly one of the digit count and the step is supplied.
preconditions.otherwise: The call fails loudly, as in the rounding function.

preconditions.condition: The divisor is not zero at the grid.
preconditions.otherwise: The whole division is undefined and the caller must guard it.

procedure: Resolve the step exactly as the rounding function does.
Round each operand onto the grid and scale it to an exact whole number by dividing by the step and taking the runtime's nearest whole number.
Take the whole quotient and the remainder of the two scaled whole numbers.
Return the quotient unchanged, and the remainder multiplied by the step and rounded onto the grid.
records.formula: scaled_dividend = nearest_whole( round_to_step( dividend , step ) ÷ step ) ; scaled_divisor = nearest_whole( round_to_step( divisor , step ) ÷ step ) ; quotient = whole_part( scaled_dividend ÷ scaled_divisor ) ; remainder = round_to_step( ( scaled_dividend − quotient × scaled_divisor ) × step , step )

rounding.what: Each operand before scaling, and the remainder after scaling back.
rounding.precision: The resolved step, one hundredth at the shipped precision.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, the default of the rounding function.
rounding.step: Operands are rounded before the whole division; the remainder is rounded after being scaled back.

result.name: whole quotient and remainder
result.unit_or_currency: the quotient is a count with no unit; the remainder is in the unit of the operands
result.stored_or_displayed: returned to the caller

edge_cases.case: The dividend is an exact multiple of the divisor but their binary representations are not.
edge_cases.outcome: The scaling to whole numbers removes the representation error, so the remainder is exactly zero.

edge_cases.case: The dividend is smaller than the divisor.
edge_cases.outcome: The quotient is zero and the remainder is the dividend rounded onto the grid.

edge_cases.case: The operands are negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole quotient and remainder follow the runtime's whole-division convention applied to the scaled whole numbers.

worked_examples.description: Eight split into packs of one and six tenths
worked_examples.narrative: Scaling to whole numbers of hundredths makes the division exact, so the remainder is zero; a direct remainder operation on the unscaled values would return about one and five thousand nine hundred ninety-nine ten-thousandths instead.

worked_examples.description: Twenty split into dozens
worked_examples.narrative: One whole dozen fits, and the remainder of eight hundred hundredths scales back to eight, satisfying the postcondition that the dividend equals the quotient multiplied by the divisor plus the remainder.

records.name: The absolute quantity of a unit
records.purpose: Derives, for every unit, how many of the root unit of its tree one of it contains. Every quantity conversion and every price conversion in the platform is a ratio of two absolute quantities.

operands.name: contained quantity of the unit
operands.unit_or_currency: a count of reference units in one of this unit, no unit of its own
operands.source: the `relative_factor` field of the Unit of Measure, typed by the user
operands.constraints: not zero; a root unit must contain exactly one

operands.name: absolute quantity of the reference unit
operands.unit_or_currency: a count of root units, no unit of its own
operands.source: the stored `factor` field of the unit named by `relative_uom_id`
operands.constraints: already computed and stored; not recomputed from the chain

preconditions.condition: The unit is not its own ancestor.
preconditions.otherwise: The recursion would not terminate; the cycle is refused by validation.

preconditions.condition: The contained quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The stored check refuses the write, because an absolute quantity of zero would make every conversion into the unit a division by zero.

procedure: If the unit has no reference unit, its absolute quantity is its contained quantity, which validation forces to be one.
Otherwise multiply the unit's contained quantity by the stored absolute quantity of its reference unit.
Store the result on the unit.
Recompute the absolute quantity of every unit below this one in the tree, in the same transaction, from the root downwards.
Use the reference unit's stored value and never a freshly evaluated product of the whole chain, because the order of multiplication changes the last digits.
records.formula: absolute_quantity(unit) = contained_quantity(unit) × absolute_quantity( reference_unit(unit) ) if the unit has a reference unit ; absolute_quantity(unit) = contained_quantity(unit) if it does not

rounding.what: Nothing; the product is stored as computed.
rounding.precision: The full precision of the stored number; no grid is applied.
rounding.method: None.
rounding.step: Not applicable; the values that are not exactly representable are stored with their representation error and are reproduced deliberately.

result.name: absolute quantity
result.unit_or_currency: a count of root units in one of this unit, no unit of its own
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on the Unit of Measure as `factor` and read by every conversion

edge_cases.case: The unit is a root unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The absolute quantity is one, because a root unit must contain exactly one.

edge_cases.case: The contained quantity is smaller than one.
edge_cases.outcome: The absolute quantity is smaller than one and the unit is finer than the root; the minute is the shipped example.

edge_cases.case: The contained quantity is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The stored check forbids only zero, so a negative contained quantity produces a negative absolute quantity and conversions into negative numbers.

edge_cases.case: A contained quantity is edited on a unit that has descendants.
edge_cases.outcome: The subtree is locked and every descendant's absolute quantity is recomputed in the same transaction.

worked_examples.description: The counting tree, root downwards
worked_examples.narrative: The counting unit is the root with an absolute quantity of one; the dozen is twelve multiplied by one; the box is twelve multiplied by the dozen's stored twelve; the pallet is forty multiplied by the box's stored one hundred forty-four.

worked_examples.description: A contained quantity smaller than one
worked_examples.narrative: The shipped contained quantity is one sixtieth rounded up at the seventh decimal digit, so an hour is fifty-nine and nine hundred ninety-nine thousandths minutes before rounding rather than exactly sixty.

records.name: The absolute quantity chain of the length tree
records.purpose: Reproduces, to the last representable digit, the stored absolute quantities of a chain whose members are not exactly representable, so that a rebuild knows which digits to expect and which discrepancies exact decimal arithmetic will introduce.

operands.name: contained quantity of each unit of the chain
operands.unit_or_currency: a count of reference units, no unit of its own
operands.source: the delivered reference data: the centimetre contains ten millimetres, the metre one hundred centimetres, the kilometre one thousand metres, the inch two and fifty-four hundredths centimetres, the foot twelve inches, the yard three feet and the mile one thousand seven hundred sixty yards

operands.name: stored absolute quantity of the reference unit
operands.unit_or_currency: a count of millimetres, no unit of its own
operands.source: the stored `factor` of the unit above in the chain
operands.constraints: the stored value, not a freshly evaluated chain

preconditions.condition: Each multiplication uses the stored value of the reference unit.
preconditions.otherwise: Collapsing the chain into one product gives exactly three hundred four and eight tenths for the foot, and the conversion matrix of the length tree no longer matches digit for digit.

procedure: Start at the millimetre, the root of the tree, whose absolute quantity is one.
Multiply ten by the millimetre's stored one to obtain the centimetre.
Multiply one hundred by the centimetre's stored ten to obtain the metre.
Multiply one thousand by the metre's stored one thousand to obtain the kilometre.
Multiply two and fifty-four hundredths by the centimetre's stored ten to obtain the inch.
Multiply twelve by the inch's stored value to obtain the foot.
Multiply three by the foot's stored value to obtain the yard.
Multiply one thousand seven hundred sixty by the yard's stored value to obtain the mile.
records.formula: absolute_quantity(mm) = 1 ; absolute_quantity(cm) = 10 × 1 = 10 ; absolute_quantity(m) = 100 × 10 = 1000 ; absolute_quantity(km) = 1000 × 1000 = 1000000 ; absolute_quantity(in) = 2.54 × 10 = 25.4 ; absolute_quantity(ft) = 12 × 25.4 = 304.79999999999995 ; absolute_quantity(yd) = 3 × 304.79999999999995 = 914.3999999999999 ; absolute_quantity(mi) = 1760 × 914.3999999999999 = 1609343.9999999998

rounding.what: Nothing; the products are stored exactly as the stated multiplication order produces them.
rounding.precision: The full precision of the stored number.
rounding.method: None.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: absolute quantity of each unit of the length tree
result.unit_or_currency: a count of millimetres, no unit of its own
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on each Unit of Measure as `factor`

edge_cases.case: A rebuild uses exact decimal arithmetic.
edge_cases.outcome: It obtains three hundred four and eight tenths for the foot, nine hundred fourteen and four tenths for the yard and one million six hundred nine thousand three hundred forty-four for the mile, rounds differently on some conversions, and must document those discrepancies; it must not expect the length rows of the conversion matrix to match digit for digit.

edge_cases.case: The chain is re-evaluated from the root on every read rather than stored.
edge_cases.outcome: The same discrepancy appears, because the multiplication order differs from the stored left-to-right chain.

worked_examples.description: The whole delivered chain
worked_examples.narrative: The three imperial values carry visible representation error because each is derived from the stored value of the unit above rather than from an exact definition.

worked_examples.description: The consequence for a single conversion
worked_examples.narrative: One foot is a hair under twelve inches before rounding; the away-from-zero method would lift a genuine excess but the compensation term absorbs this representation error, so the answer is exactly twelve.

operands.unit_or_currency: a count of root units, no unit of its own

operands.unit_or_currency: a count of root units, no unit of its own

preconditions.otherwise: The division has no divisor and the new unit cannot be positioned in the tree.

Divide it by the stored absolute quantity of the unit chosen as reference.
Type the quotient as the contained quantity of the new unit.

rounding.what: Nothing; the quotient is typed as it stands.
rounding.precision: The full precision of the stored number.
rounding.method: None.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: contained quantity to type
result.unit_or_currency: a count of reference units in one of the new unit, no unit of its own
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on the new Unit of Measure as `relative_factor`

edge_cases.case: The chosen reference unit is the root.
edge_cases.outcome: The contained quantity equals the desired absolute quantity, because the root's absolute quantity is one.

edge_cases.case: The quotient is smaller than one.
edge_cases.outcome: Legal; the new unit is finer than its reference unit.

edge_cases.outcome: Refused by the stored check on the contained quantity.

worked_examples.narrative: One hundred forty-four divided by twelve is twelve, so the new unit is declared as containing twelve dozens.

records.name: The quantity ladder of the counting tree
records.purpose: Gives one of each counting unit expressed in every other, so that a rebuild can check its stored absolute quantities against a single table before running any conversion.

operands.name: absolute quantity of the source unit
operands.unit_or_currency: a count of counting units, no unit of its own
operands.source: the stored `factor` of the unit being expressed

operands.name: absolute quantity of the destination unit
operands.unit_or_currency: a count of counting units, no unit of its own
operands.source: the stored `factor` of the unit it is expressed in

preconditions.condition: Both units belong to the counting tree.
preconditions.otherwise: The ratio has no physical meaning; the shared-ancestor test is the caller's guard.

Divide it by the absolute quantity of the unit it is expressed in.
Read the quotient as the number of destination units in one source unit.

rounding.what: Nothing in the ladder itself; the ladder states exact ratios, and rounding happens only when the conversion operation is called.
rounding.precision: Not applicable to the ladder.
rounding.method: None.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.stored_or_displayed: displayed as reference; recomputed by every conversion

edge_cases.case: The source and destination units coincide.
edge_cases.outcome: The ratio is one, the diagonal of the ladder.

edge_cases.case: The destination unit is much larger than the source unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The exact ratio is a small fraction that the conversion operation will inflate to one step under away-from-zero rounding.

worked_examples.description: Each counting unit expressed in the others
worked_examples.narrative: A pallet is five thousand seven hundred sixty items, four hundred eighty dozens, nine hundred sixty packs of six or forty boxes; a box is one hundred forty-four items, twelve dozens or twenty-four packs of six.

worked_examples.description: The fractions read the other way
worked_examples.narrative: One item is a sixth of a pack, a twelfth of a dozen, a one-hundred-forty-fourth of a box and a one-five-thousand-seven-hundred-sixtieth of a pallet, before any rounding is applied.

records.name: The quantity conversion algorithm
records.purpose: The operation every document boundary calls to express a quantity in a different unit. It scales by the two absolute quantities in a fixed order and rounds onto the destination unit's grid.

operands.name: quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity expressed in the source unit
operands.source: the calling document line, move or report

operands.name: source unit
operands.unit_or_currency: exactly one Unit of Measure, or none
operands.source: the record holding the quantity
operands.constraints: exactly one record when present; more than one, or an unloaded set, is a programming error

operands.name: destination unit
operands.unit_or_currency: one Unit of Measure, or none
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: may be absent, in which case the result is expressed in the root unit of the source unit's tree

operands.name: rounding method
operands.unit_or_currency: one of the five methods, no unit
operands.source: the caller; this operation defaults to away from zero

operands.name: raise on failure
operands.unit_or_currency: true or false, no unit
operands.source: the caller; the default is true
operands.constraints: decides whether an impossible conversion fails or returns the input unchanged

preconditions.condition: The source is exactly one unit.
preconditions.otherwise: The assertion fails; more than one unit, or an unloaded set, is a programming error.

preconditions.condition: The caller has checked that the two units share an ancestor when the result must be meaningful.
preconditions.otherwise: The operation performs no tree check and will return a number with no physical meaning.

procedure: If there is no source unit, or the quantity is zero, return the quantity unchanged with no rounding and no unit check.
Assert that the source is exactly one unit.
If the source unit and the destination unit are the same record, take the quantity itself as the working amount, with no multiplication and no division.
Otherwise multiply the quantity by the absolute quantity of the source unit.
Then, only if a destination unit was supplied, divide by the absolute quantity of the destination unit; the order is fixed, multiply first and divide second.

If a destination unit was supplied and rounding was requested, round the amount onto the destination unit's rounding precision with the supplied method, which is the `Product Unit` step because every unit shares one precision.
Return the amount.
records.formula: amount = quantity × absolute_quantity( source_unit ) ; amount = amount ÷ absolute_quantity( destination_unit ) only if a destination unit was supplied ; result = round_to_step( amount , rounding_precision( destination_unit ) , rounding_method )

rounding.what: The scaled amount, once both factors have been applied.
rounding.precision: The destination unit's rounding precision, which is the `Product Unit` step, one hundredth as shipped.
rounding.method: Away from zero by default; half away from zero, towards zero, half towards zero or half to even when the caller names them.
rounding.step: After the multiplication and the division, and only when a destination unit was supplied and rounding was requested.

result.name: quantity in the destination unit
result.unit_or_currency: the destination unit, or the root unit of the source tree when no destination was supplied
result.stored_or_displayed: returned to the caller, which stores or displays it according to the boundary

edge_cases.case: A rebuild computes the ratio of the two absolute quantities first and multiplies once.
edge_cases.outcome: Different last digits on many pairs; the multiplication must come first and the division second.

edge_cases.case: No destination unit is supplied.
edge_cases.outcome: The quantity is expressed in the root unit of the source unit's tree and no rounding happens at all, even when rounding was requested.

edge_cases.case: The two units are in different trees.
edge_cases.outcome: No check is performed; the arithmetic runs and produces a meaningless number unless the caller guarded it.

edge_cases.case: The quantity is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: Converted by the same formula with no special case; the rounding methods are symmetric about zero.

worked_examples.description: Two and a half dozens into units
worked_examples.narrative: The exact value lands on the grid, so every rounding method returns thirty.

worked_examples.description: Seven units into dozens
worked_examples.narrative: Fifty-eight and one third steps is pushed to fifty-nine steps by the default method, so seven items are reported as fifty-nine hundredths of a dozen.

records.name: Quantity conversion of zero or with no source unit
records.purpose: The two short-circuits that return the input untouched, so that a rebuild never rounds a zero into a step and never fails on a line that carries no unit.

operands.name: quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the source unit, or in no unit at all
operands.source: the calling record
operands.constraints: the short-circuit fires when the quantity is zero or otherwise empty

operands.name: source unit
operands.unit_or_currency: one Unit of Measure, or none
operands.source: the calling record
operands.constraints: the short-circuit fires when there is none

preconditions.condition: The short-circuit is tested before the single-record assertion.
preconditions.otherwise: A display-only line, which holds no unit, would fail the assertion instead of returning its quantity.

procedure: If there is no source unit, return the quantity unchanged, unrounded, whatever destination unit was named.
If the quantity is zero, or otherwise empty, return it unchanged, unrounded, whatever the units and whatever the rounding method.
records.formula: result = quantity when source_unit is absent ; result = quantity when quantity = 0

rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.method: None; the rounding step is never reached.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: quantity, unchanged
result.unit_or_currency: the unit it arrived in, if any
result.stored_or_displayed: returned to the caller

edge_cases.case: A conversion of zero between units of different trees.
edge_cases.outcome: Zero, because the short-circuit runs before any tree consideration.

edge_cases.case: A display-only document line, which holds no unit.
edge_cases.outcome: Its quantity passes through unchanged.

edge_cases.case: A negative zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Treated as empty by the short-circuit and returned unchanged.

worked_examples.description: A quantity on a line with no unit
worked_examples.narrative: With no source unit the input is returned unchanged and unrounded.

records.name: Quantity conversion when the source and destination units coincide
records.purpose: States what a conversion to a unit's own unit does: it skips the factor arithmetic but still rounds, which is how a quantity gets snapped onto the grid without being scaled.

operands.name: quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the unit that is both source and destination
operands.source: the calling record
operands.constraints: not zero, or the zero short-circuit fires first

operands.name: rounding method
operands.unit_or_currency: one of the five methods, no unit
operands.source: the caller; away from zero by default

preconditions.condition: The source unit and the destination unit are the same record.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary scaling path runs.

procedure: Take the quantity itself as the working amount, performing no multiplication and no division.
Round the amount onto the `Product Unit` grid with the requested method.
Return the rounded amount.

rounding.precision: The `Product Unit` step, one hundredth as shipped.
rounding.method: The requested method; away from zero when the caller does not name one.
rounding.step: After the factor arithmetic is skipped.

result.name: quantity in the same unit, snapped onto the grid
result.stored_or_displayed: returned to the caller

edge_cases.outcome: The rounding step still runs and moves it onto the grid.

operands.name: quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the source unit

records.name: The price list rule formula with unit conversion in place
records.purpose: States the complete price of a rule of the formula kind with every unit scaling shown, so that a rebuild applies the price conversion to the base, the surcharge and the two margins and to none of the percentages.

operands.name: price of the chosen base
operands.unit_or_currency: an amount in the target currency, per one destination unit
operands.source: the catalogue price, the cost or another price list, expressed per the destination unit, converted to the target currency and unrounded

operands.name: discount percentage
operands.unit_or_currency: a percentage, no currency
operands.source: the price list rule; replaced by the negated markup when the base is the cost

operands.name: price rounding step
operands.unit_or_currency: an amount in the target currency
operands.source: the price list rule, when one is configured

operands.name: surcharge
operands.unit_or_currency: an amount in the target currency, per one of the product's own unit
operands.source: the price list rule, when one is configured

operands.name: minimum margin and maximum margin
operands.unit_or_currency: amounts in the target currency, per one of the product's own unit
operands.source: the price list rule, when configured

preconditions.condition: The base price is already expressed per the destination unit and in the target currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The discount, the surcharge and the margins are applied to a price in the wrong unit and the line total is wrong by the ratio of the two absolute quantities.

preconditions.condition: The surcharge and the two margins are understood as amounts per the product's own unit.
preconditions.otherwise: They are added at the wrong scale.

procedure: Take the price of the chosen base, expressed per the destination unit, converted to the target currency, unrounded.
Subtract the discount percentage of that base price; when the base is the cost, the discount is the negated markup.
If a rounding step is configured, round the price onto that step.
If a surcharge is configured, add the surcharge converted from the product's own unit to the destination unit.
If a minimum margin is configured, take the larger of the price and the base price plus the converted minimum margin.
If a maximum margin is configured, take the smaller of the price and the base price plus the converted maximum margin.
records.formula: base_price = price_of_the_chosen_base , expressed per destination_unit , converted to the target currency , unrounded ; price = base_price − ( base_price × discount_percentage ÷ 100 ) ; price = round_to_step( price , price_rounding_step ) if a rounding step is configured ; price = price + convert_price( surcharge , product_unit → destination_unit ) if a surcharge is configured ; price = max( price , base_price + convert_price( minimum_margin , product_unit → destination_unit ) ) if a minimum margin is configured ; price = min( price , base_price + convert_price( maximum_margin , product_unit → destination_unit ) ) if a maximum margin is configured

rounding.what: Only the price, and only when the rule configures a price rounding step.
rounding.precision: The configured price rounding step of the rule; the unit conversions inside the formula never round.
rounding.method: The rounding function's own default, half away from zero.
rounding.step: After the discount and before the surcharge and the margins.

result.name: price per destination unit
result.unit_or_currency: an amount in the target currency, per one destination unit
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed on the document line as its unit price

edge_cases.outcome: The price carries the full precision of the base into the surcharge and margin steps.

edge_cases.case: Both margins are configured and conflict.
edge_cases.outcome: The maximum margin is applied last, so a ceiling below the floor wins.

records.name: Whole-packaging rounding
records.purpose: Snaps a quantity, expressed in a product's own unit, onto a whole multiple of a packaging quantity, for a business that refuses to break a carton.

operands.name: packaging unit
operands.unit_or_currency: one Unit of Measure, the unit whose whole multiples the result must be
operands.source: the unit the operation is invoked on, which comes from the move's packaging unit

operands.name: product quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the destination unit, in practice the product's own unit
operands.source: the reservation
operands.constraints: a real number; zero returns unchanged

operands.name: destination unit
operands.unit_or_currency: one Unit of Measure, in practice the product's own unit
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: the unit the quantity is expressed in

operands.name: rounding method
operands.unit_or_currency: one of away from zero, half away from zero or towards zero, no unit
operands.source: the caller; the operation's own default is half away from zero and the only caller passes towards zero

preconditions.condition: The packaging unit is exactly one unit.
preconditions.otherwise: The assertion fails as a programming error.

preconditions.condition: Both the product quantity and the packaging quantity are non-zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The product quantity is returned unchanged.

procedure: Assert the packaging unit is exactly one unit.
Compute the packaging quantity by converting a quantity of one from the packaging unit into the destination unit with the default away-from-zero rounding at the `Product Unit` precision.
If the packaging unit and the destination unit are the same record, return the product quantity unchanged; this test happens after the packaging quantity is computed and before it is used.

If both the product quantity and the packaging quantity are non-zero, divide the product quantity by the packaging quantity, round that quotient onto a step of one with the requested method, and multiply the whole number back by the packaging quantity.
Otherwise return the product quantity unchanged.
records.formula: packaging_quantity = convert_quantity( 1 , packaging_unit → destination_unit ) ; result = round_to_step( product_quantity ÷ packaging_quantity , step = 1 , rounding_method ) × packaging_quantity

rounding.what: The quotient of the product quantity by the packaging quantity, and separately the packaging quantity itself.
rounding.precision: A step of one for the quotient, so that the result is a whole number of packagings; the `Product Unit` step for the packaging quantity.
rounding.method: The requested method for the quotient, which the only caller sets to towards zero; away from zero for the packaging quantity.
rounding.step: The quotient is rounded before being multiplied back.

result.stored_or_displayed: returned to the reservation, which reserves that quantity

edge_cases.outcome: Returned unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The packaging quantity rounds to zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Returned unchanged, because a packaging quantity of zero is empty.

edge_cases.case: A rebuild tests a remainder instead of dividing, rounding and multiplying.

edge_cases.outcome: The result can exceed what exists, which is why the reservation caller never uses it.
