procedure: Take the quantity produced by the second leg of the double conversion.
Test whether it is a whole number at the `Product Unit` precision.
If it is not, reduce the reservation to zero.
records.formula: reserved = 0 when the product is serial-tracked and quantity_after_double_conversion is not a whole number at the Product Unit precision ; reserved = quantity_after_double_conversion otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing further; the test is made at the `Product Unit` precision on a quantity that has already been rounded twice.
rounding.precision: One hundredth at the shipped two digits.
rounding.method: None; the test is a whole-number test.
rounding.step: After the second leg of the double conversion.

result.name: quantity reserved for a serial-tracked product
result.stored_or_displayed: used by the reservation

edge_cases.case: The double conversion produced fifty-seven and ninety-six hundredths.
edge_cases.outcome: Not a whole number, so nothing is reserved for a serial-tracked product.

edge_cases.case: The double conversion produced sixty.
edge_cases.outcome: A whole number, so sixty are reserved and sixty serial numbers are expected.

edge_cases.case: The product is lot-tracked rather than serial-tracked.
edge_cases.outcome: The reduction does not apply; a lot may hold a fractional quantity.

worked_examples.description: A serial-tracked product with fifty-eight units available and a move in boxes of twelve
worked_examples.narrative: The double conversion cannot land on a whole number here, so a serial-tracked product reserves nothing at all.

worked_examples.description: The same product with sixty units available
worked_examples.narrative: Sixty is a whole number of items and five whole boxes, so the reservation stands.

records.name: The relabelling that follows a change of a product's own unit
records.purpose: States the arithmetic of a unit change on a product: there is none. Every stored number stays as it was and only the unit reference is replaced, which a rebuild must reproduce exactly rather than recomputing quantities.

operands.name: stored quantity on each impacted record
operands.unit_or_currency: the old unit of the product
operands.source: stock moves, move lines, quantities on hand and every other record holding the product's quantity

operands.name: old unit and new unit
operands.unit_or_currency: two Units of Measure
operands.source: the product before and after the change
operands.constraints: the change is refused when another unit is already in use on an open document or on a posted journal item

preconditions.condition: The change is permitted: no other unit is already in use and no posted invoice holds another unit.
preconditions.otherwise: The change is refused with the messages the business rules state.

procedure: Replace the unit reference on the impacted records.
Leave every stored number exactly as it was.
State the consequence to the user before the change, as a conversion of one old unit to one new unit.
Do not recompute the real quantity of existing moves, the quantity in the product's unit of existing move lines, or any quantity on hand.
records.formula: new_quantity = old_quantity ; one old unit = one new unit

rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.method: None.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the same stored numbers under a new unit
result.unit_or_currency: the new unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: stored unchanged on every impacted record

edge_cases.case: A move for sixty whose product changes from `Units` to `kg` (kilogram).
edge_cases.outcome: It becomes a move for sixty kilograms; the number does not change.

edge_cases.case: A rebuild that converts on the unit change.
edge_cases.outcome: Quantities on hand, move real quantities and move line quantities all diverge from the specification; the operation is a relabelling, not a conversion.

edge_cases.case: A posted journal item holding a different unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The change is refused, because the posted item would then disagree with its product.

worked_examples.description: A product whose own unit changes while a move exists

expected_outputs.quantity_on_hand_after: unchanged in number, relabelled in unit
expected_outputs.message_shown_to_the_user: a conversion of one old unit equals one new unit

worked_examples.narrative: Nothing is converted; the number sixty now means sixty kilograms.

records.name: The sequence of a unit
records.purpose: Derives the ordering position of a unit from its contained quantity, so that units of a tree list from the finest to the coarsest without a user typing an order.

operands.name: contained quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: a count of reference units in one of this unit, no unit of its own
operands.source: the `relative_factor` field of the Unit of Measure

preconditions.condition: The record is new, or its sequence is zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The derivation does not run and the stored sequence is kept.

procedure: Multiply the contained quantity by one hundred.
Truncate the product towards zero to a whole number.
Take the smaller of one thousand and that whole number.
Store the result as the unit's sequence.
records.formula: sequence = minimum( 1000 , truncate_towards_zero( contained_quantity × 100 ) )

rounding.what: The product of the contained quantity and one hundred.
rounding.precision: A whole number.
rounding.method: Truncation towards zero.
rounding.step: Before the cap of one thousand is applied.

result.name: sequence
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on the Unit of Measure as `sequence` and used to order lists

edge_cases.case: A contained quantity of twelve or more.
edge_cases.outcome: The product exceeds one thousand and the cap applies, so every coarse unit shares the sequence of one thousand.

edge_cases.case: A contained quantity smaller than one hundredth.
edge_cases.outcome: The truncation gives zero and the unit sorts first.

edge_cases.case: The record already carries a non-zero sequence.
edge_cases.outcome: The derivation does not run and the stored sequence stands.

worked_examples.description: The seven values the document states
worked_examples.narrative: Twelve gives one thousand capped from one thousand two hundred, and twenty-eight and three thousand four hundred ninety-five ten-thousandths gives one thousand capped from two thousand eight hundred thirty-four.

worked_examples.description: The two configured packaging units
worked_examples.narrative: Both exceed the cap, so both take the sequence of one thousand.

records.name: The rounding precision of a unit
records.purpose: Gives every unit the same grid, derived from one global decimal precision record rather than from anything on the unit itself.

operands.name: digits of the `Product Unit` decimal precision record
operands.unit_or_currency: a count of decimal digits, no unit
operands.source: the decimal precision record whose usage is `Product Unit`
operands.constraints: a whole number greater than or equal to zero; two as shipped

preconditions.condition: The `Product Unit` decimal precision record exists.
preconditions.otherwise: The lookup falls back to two digits, which silently restores the shipped behaviour.

procedure: Read the digit count of the `Product Unit` decimal precision record, through the cache.
Raise ten to the power of the negated digit count.
Report the result as the rounding precision of the unit; every unit reports the same value.
records.formula: rounding_precision = 10 ^ ( − digits_of( "Product Unit" ) )

rounding.what: Nothing; the operation produces the grid other operations round onto.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.method: None.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: rounding precision of the unit
result.unit_or_currency: a fraction of one unit, no currency
result.stored_or_displayed: reported by the `rounding` field of every Unit of Measure and read by every conversion

edge_cases.case: The precision record is deleted.
edge_cases.outcome: Two digits are used, so every unit reports one hundredth again.

edge_cases.case: The precision record is changed.
edge_cases.outcome: Every unit's reported precision changes at once, and the cache must be cleared on the create, the write and the delete of any decimal precision record or conversions keep using the old value until the process restarts.

edge_cases.case: A rebuild stores a precision per unit.
edge_cases.outcome: It diverges from the specification, in which units are never company scoped and every unit shares one precision.

worked_examples.description: The shipped configuration
worked_examples.narrative: All thirty delivered units report one hundredth, whatever their tree or their absolute quantity.

worked_examples.description: The record removed
worked_examples.narrative: An unknown usage means two digits, so removing the record silently restores the shipped grid.

records.name: The discounted vendor price
records.purpose: Turns a vendor's quoted price, expressed per the vendor's own unit, into a discounted price per the product's own unit, which is the figure every purchase-side computation starts from.

operands.name: vendor price
operands.unit_or_currency: an amount in the vendor price list's currency, per one vendor unit
operands.source: the vendor price list line

operands.name: vendor unit
operands.unit_or_currency: one Unit of Measure
operands.source: the vendor price list line; it need not be among the product's additional units
operands.constraints: shares an ancestor with the product's own unit

operands.name: product's own unit
operands.unit_or_currency: one Unit of Measure
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: the destination of the price conversion

operands.name: discount percentage
operands.unit_or_currency: a percentage, no currency
operands.source: the vendor price list line

preconditions.condition: The price conversion is applied before the discount.
preconditions.otherwise: The discount is taken at the wrong scale only when the discount is an amount rather than a percentage; with a percentage the order does not change the result but the specification fixes it for reproducibility.

procedure: Convert the vendor price from the vendor's unit into the product's own unit with the price conversion, which never rounds.
Multiply by one minus the discount percentage divided by one hundred.
Return the discounted price per the product's own unit, unrounded.
records.formula: discounted_price = convert_price( vendor_price , vendor_unit → product_own_unit ) × ( 1 − discount_percentage ÷ 100 )

rounding.precision: Not applicable; the caller rounds to its currency.
rounding.method: None.
rounding.step: The first rounding happens when the purchase line rounds to its currency.

result.name: discounted vendor price per the product's own unit
result.unit_or_currency: an amount in the vendor price list's currency, per one of the product's own unit
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed on the vendor price list line and used by the purchase line

edge_cases.case: The vendor unit and the product's own unit coincide.
edge_cases.outcome: The price conversion short-circuits and only the discount applies.

edge_cases.case: The discount is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The converted price is returned unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The vendor quotes in a unit that is not among the product's additional units.
edge_cases.outcome: Allowed; the purchase line's allowed list includes vendor units.

worked_examples.description: One hundred twenty per box of twelve dozens with a five per cent discount
worked_examples.narrative: The unrounded discounted price per item is seventy-nine and one sixth hundredths, which multiplied by one hundred forty-four gives one hundred fourteen, the discounted box price.

records.name: The purchase order line total quantity
records.purpose: Restates the ordered quantity of a purchase line in the product's own unit, which is the figure the accrual, the three-way match and the valuation all use.

operands.name: ordered quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the purchase line's unit
operands.source: the purchase order line

operands.name: line unit
operands.unit_or_currency: one Unit of Measure
operands.source: the purchase order line
operands.constraints: on the allowed list, which includes vendor units

operands.name: product's own unit
operands.unit_or_currency: one Unit of Measure
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: shares an ancestor with the line unit

preconditions.condition: The two units differ.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordered quantity is taken as the total quantity with no conversion at all.

procedure: If the line unit and the product's own unit are the same, take the ordered quantity as the total quantity.
Otherwise convert the ordered quantity from the line's unit into the product's own unit with the default away-from-zero rounding.
Store the result on the line.
records.formula: total_quantity = convert_quantity( ordered_quantity , line_unit → product_own_unit ) if the units differ ; total_quantity = ordered_quantity if they are the same

rounding.precision: One hundredth, the `Product Unit` step at the shipped two digits.
rounding.method: Away from zero, because the result is a commercial quantity that must not under-serve the counterparty.
rounding.step: Once, when the line is written.

result.name: total quantity
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on the purchase order line and read by the accrual and by three-way matching

edge_cases.case: The units coincide.
edge_cases.outcome: No conversion at all, not even a re-rounding onto the grid.

edge_cases.case: The line quantity is fractional.
edge_cases.outcome: The converted quantity is rounded away from zero, so the stored total may exceed the exact value by up to one hundredth.

edge_cases.case: The line unit is in a different tree from the product's own unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The line's allowed list prevents this; the unit must be one of the product's allowed units or a vendor unit.

worked_examples.description: Seven boxes of twelve
worked_examples.narrative: Seven boxes of twelve are eighty-four units, exactly on the grid.

worked_examples.description: A line already in the product's own unit
worked_examples.narrative: When the units coincide the ordered quantity is taken as it stands, so an off-grid quantity is not snapped by this crossing.

records.name: The purchase order line gross unit price in the product's unit
records.purpose: Reduces a purchase line's price to a price per one of the product's own unit, after discount and after tax exclusion, so that an accrual can be valued against a quantity expressed in that same unit.

operands.name: line price
operands.unit_or_currency: an amount in the order's currency, per one line unit
operands.source: the purchase order line

operands.name: discount percentage
operands.unit_or_currency: a percentage, no currency
operands.source: the purchase order line
operands.constraints: applied only when a discount is present

operands.name: quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the line's unit
operands.source: the purchase order line
operands.constraints: used only for the tax-exclusion step, where the tax-exclusive total is divided by it

operands.name: absolute quantity of the product's own unit and of the line unit
operands.unit_or_currency: counts of root units, no unit of their own
operands.source: the stored `factor` fields

preconditions.condition: The four steps are applied in the stated order.
preconditions.otherwise: A tax computed on an already-scaled price, or a discount taken after tax exclusion, gives a different accrual amount.

preconditions.condition: The quantity is not zero when taxes apply.
preconditions.otherwise: The division by the quantity in the tax-exclusion step is undefined.

procedure: Start from the line's price.
If a discount applies, multiply by one minus the discount percentage divided by one hundred.
If taxes apply, take the tax-exclusive total of that price for the line quantity and divide it by the quantity, giving a tax-exclusive price per one line unit.

If the units differ, multiply by the absolute quantity of the product's own unit and divide by the absolute quantity of the line's unit; this performs the price conversion inline, using the ratio of the two absolute quantities directly rather than calling the price conversion operation, and the arithmetic is identical.
records.formula: price = price_unit ; price = price × ( 1 − discount_percentage ÷ 100 ) if a discount applies ; price = tax_exclusive_total( price , quantity ) ÷ quantity if taxes apply ; price = price × absolute_quantity( product_own_unit ) ÷ absolute_quantity( line_unit ) if the units differ

rounding.what: Nothing inside this computation; the tax-exclusive total carries whatever rounding the tax domain applied to it.
rounding.precision: Not applicable here.
rounding.method: None.
rounding.step: The accrual amount is rounded by the reporting domain that posts it.

result.name: gross unit price per the product's own unit
result.unit_or_currency: an amount in the order's currency, per one of the product's own unit
result.stored_or_displayed: used by the accrual computation; not stored on the line

edge_cases.case: The line unit and the product's own unit coincide.
edge_cases.outcome: The last step is skipped and the price stands as the tax-exclusive discounted price.

edge_cases.case: No discount and no taxes.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the unit scaling applies.

edge_cases.case: A rebuild that calls the price conversion operation instead of scaling inline.
edge_cases.outcome: The same number, because the two forms are arithmetically identical.

worked_examples.description: One hundred twenty per box of twelve dozens, five per cent discount, no tax
worked_examples.narrative: The gross price per item is seventy-nine and one sixth hundredths, which multiplied by one hundred forty-four returns the discounted box price of one hundred fourteen.

records.name: The packaging quantity on a stock move
records.purpose: Expresses a move's demand in the packaging unit that came from the originating document line, which is the figure a delivery note prints as a number of cartons or pallets.

operands.name: demand
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the move's unit
operands.source: the stock move

operands.name: move unit
operands.unit_or_currency: one Unit of Measure
operands.source: the stock move
operands.constraints: shares an ancestor with the packaging unit

operands.name: packaging unit
operands.unit_or_currency: one Unit of Measure
operands.source: the move's packaging unit, set from the originating document line's unit
operands.constraints: the computation runs only when a packaging unit is set

preconditions.condition: A packaging unit is set on the move.
preconditions.otherwise: No packaging quantity is computed.

procedure: Convert the move's demand from the move's unit into the packaging unit.
Use the conversion default, away from zero, at the `Product Unit` precision.
Store the result as the move's packaging quantity.
records.formula: packaging_quantity = convert_quantity( demand , move_unit → packaging_unit )

rounding.precision: One hundredth, the `Product Unit` step at the shipped two digits.
rounding.method: Away from zero, because a packaging count on a delivery note must not under-serve the counterparty.
rounding.step: Once, when the move is written.

result.name: packaging quantity
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on the stock move and printed on the delivery note

edge_cases.case: The move's unit and the packaging unit coincide.
edge_cases.outcome: The identity short-circuit of the conversion applies and the demand is only re-rounded onto the grid.

edge_cases.case: A single item against a pallet.
edge_cases.outcome: One hundredth of a pallet is the system's honest answer under away-from-zero rounding; a rebuild that prints packaging quantities must expect it.

edge_cases.case: The demand is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The packaging quantity is zero, by the zero short-circuit of the conversion.

worked_examples.description: The four cases the document tabulates, for a move whose unit is `Units`
worked_examples.narrative: Fifty-eight units are four and eighty-three and one third hundredths boxes exactly, lifted to four and eighty-four hundredths by the away-from-zero default.

records.name: The bulk weight of a transfer
records.purpose: Sums the weight of everything in a transfer that is not inside a package, by converting each group of move lines into the product's own unit before multiplying by the product's weight.

operands.name: grouped quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the move line's unit
operands.source: the move lines of the transfer, grouped by transfer, product, move line unit and quantity

operands.name: line count of the group
operands.unit_or_currency: a count of move lines, no unit
operands.source: the grouping
operands.constraints: a whole number greater than zero

operands.name: product weight
operands.unit_or_currency: a weight per one of the product's own unit, interpreted as kilograms or as pounds by the system parameter that names the weight unit
operands.source: the product record

preconditions.condition: Only move lines with no destination package contribute.
preconditions.otherwise: Packaged goods would be counted twice, once in the bulk weight and once in the package weight.

procedure: Group the move lines of the transfer by transfer, product, move line unit and quantity.
Discard every group whose move lines have a destination package.
For each remaining group, convert the grouped quantity from the move line's unit into the product's own unit with the default away-from-zero rounding.
Multiply the converted quantity by the number of lines in the group and by the product's weight.
Sum the products over all groups.
records.formula: bulk_weight = Σ over groups of ( line_count × convert_quantity( grouped_quantity , move_line_unit → product_own_unit ) × product_weight )

rounding.what: The converted quantity of each group.
rounding.precision: One hundredth, the `Product Unit` step at the shipped two digits.
rounding.method: Away from zero.
rounding.step: Once per group, before the multiplication by the line count and the weight.

result.name: bulk weight
result.unit_or_currency: a weight in the unit the system parameter names, either kilograms or pounds
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed on the transfer and used by the shipping weight

edge_cases.case: Every move line has a destination package.
edge_cases.outcome: The bulk weight is zero and the whole weight comes from the packages.

edge_cases.case: The product has no weight.
edge_cases.outcome: The group contributes nothing.

edge_cases.case: Several move lines share a product, a unit and a quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: They form one group and the converted quantity is multiplied by the line count rather than converted once per line.

worked_examples.description: Three move lines of five boxes of twelve for a product weighing two
worked_examples.narrative: The group is this transfer, this product, the box of twelve and a quantity of five, with a count of three; sixty items each weighing two, three times over, is three hundred sixty.

records.name: The computed weight of a package
records.purpose: Gives the weight of one package when no shipping weight has been declared on it, as the tare of its package type plus the weight of its contents.

operands.name: tare weight of the package type
operands.unit_or_currency: a weight in the unit the system parameter names
operands.source: the package type record
operands.constraints: unchecked; a negative tare is not refused

operands.name: quantity of each contained move line
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the move line's unit
operands.source: the move lines whose destination package is this package

operands.name: product weight
operands.unit_or_currency: a weight per one of the product's own unit
operands.source: the product record of each contained line

preconditions.condition: No shipping weight has been declared on the package.
preconditions.otherwise: The declared shipping weight is used instead of the computed one.

procedure: Take the tare weight of the package's package type.
Restrict the content-weight sum to the move lines whose destination package is this package.
For each such group, convert the quantity from the move line's unit into the product's own unit away from zero and multiply by the product's weight.
Add the sum of those products to the tare weight.
records.formula: computed_package_weight = tare_weight( package_type ) + Σ over contained groups of ( line_count × convert_quantity( grouped_quantity , move_line_unit → product_own_unit ) × product_weight )

rounding.what: The converted quantity of each contained group.
rounding.precision: One hundredth, the `Product Unit` step at the shipped two digits.
rounding.method: Away from zero.
rounding.step: Once per group, before the multiplication by the weight.

result.name: computed package weight
result.unit_or_currency: a weight in the unit the system parameter names, either kilograms or pounds
result.stored_or_displayed: used by the shipping weight of the transfer when no shipping weight is declared on the package

edge_cases.case: The package type has no tare weight.
edge_cases.outcome: The computed weight is the content weight alone.

edge_cases.case: The tare weight is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: Accepted; the tare weight is unchecked, unlike the dimensions and the maximum weight, which must not be negative.

edge_cases.case: The package holds nested packages.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the outermost destination packages are summed by the transfer, so a nested package contributes through its parent.

worked_examples.description: A carton of tare one holding sixty items weighing two each
worked_examples.narrative: One for the carton itself plus one hundred twenty for its contents.

records.name: The shipping weight of a transfer
records.purpose: Gives the total weight a carrier will handle: the bulk weight of the unpackaged goods plus the weight of every outermost package.

operands.name: bulk weight
operands.unit_or_currency: a weight in the unit the system parameter names
operands.source: the bulk weight computation of the same transfer

operands.name: declared shipping weight of each outermost destination package
operands.unit_or_currency: a weight in the same unit
operands.source: the package record, when a weight has been declared
operands.constraints: used in preference to the computed weight

operands.name: computed weight of each outermost destination package
operands.unit_or_currency: a weight in the same unit
operands.source: the package type's tare plus the content-weight sum restricted to that package
operands.constraints: used when no shipping weight is declared

preconditions.condition: Only the outermost destination packages are summed.
preconditions.otherwise: A nested package would be counted twice.

procedure: Take the bulk weight of the transfer, which covers every move line with no destination package.
For each outermost destination package, take its declared shipping weight when one exists, and otherwise its computed weight.
Add those package weights to the bulk weight.
records.formula: shipping_weight = bulk_weight + Σ over outermost destination packages of ( declared_shipping_weight or computed_package_weight )

rounding.what: Nothing beyond the rounding already applied inside the bulk weight and the computed package weights.
rounding.precision: One hundredth on each contained quantity conversion.
rounding.method: Away from zero on each conversion.
rounding.step: Inside each contributing weight, never on the sum.

result.name: shipping weight
result.unit_or_currency: a weight in the unit the system parameter names, either kilograms or pounds
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed on the transfer and handed to the delivery method

edge_cases.case: Nothing is packaged.
edge_cases.outcome: The shipping weight equals the bulk weight.

edge_cases.case: Everything is packaged.
edge_cases.outcome: The bulk weight is zero and the shipping weight is the sum of the package weights.

edge_cases.case: A package declares a shipping weight that disagrees with its contents.
edge_cases.outcome: The declared weight wins; the computed weight is only a fallback.

worked_examples.description: A transfer with three unpackaged lines and one carton
worked_examples.narrative: Three hundred sixty for the bulk goods plus one hundred twenty-one for the carton.

worked_examples.description: The same transfer with a declared package weight
worked_examples.narrative: The declared weight replaces the computed one.

records.name: The shipping volume of a transfer
records.purpose: Sums the volume of everything picked on a transfer, by converting each move's picked quantity into the product's own unit before multiplying by the product's volume.

operands.name: picked quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the move's unit
operands.source: each stock move of the transfer

operands.name: move unit
operands.unit_or_currency: one Unit of Measure
operands.source: the stock move
operands.constraints: shares an ancestor with the product's own unit

operands.name: product volume
operands.unit_or_currency: a volume per one of the product's own unit
operands.source: the product record

preconditions.condition: Each move's picked quantity is converted before being multiplied by the volume.
preconditions.otherwise: A move counted in boxes would contribute the volume of a single item per box.

procedure: For each move of the transfer, convert the picked quantity from the move's unit into the product's own unit with the default away-from-zero rounding.
Multiply the converted quantity by the product's volume.
Sum the products over all moves.
records.formula: shipping_volume = Σ over moves of ( convert_quantity( picked_quantity , move_unit → product_own_unit ) × product_volume )

rounding.what: The converted picked quantity of each move.
rounding.precision: One hundredth, the `Product Unit` step at the shipped two digits.
rounding.method: Away from zero.
rounding.step: Once per move, before the multiplication by the volume.

result.name: shipping volume
result.unit_or_currency: a volume in the unit the product's volume is expressed in
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed on the transfer and handed to the delivery method

edge_cases.case: A move has not been picked.
edge_cases.outcome: Its picked quantity is zero and it contributes nothing, by the zero short-circuit of the conversion.

edge_cases.case: The product has no volume.
edge_cases.outcome: The move contributes nothing.

edge_cases.case: The move's unit is the product's own unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion is an identity apart from the rounding onto the grid.

worked_examples.description: One move of five boxes of twelve for a product of volume three thousandths
worked_examples.narrative: Sixty items at three thousandths each is eighteen hundredths of a volume unit.

records.name: The content description of a package
records.purpose: Renders the contents of a package for display, deciding whether a quantity prints with a decimal part and whether the unit's name appears at all.

operands.name: quantity of each group
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the group's unit
operands.source: the contents of the package, grouped by unit and product

operands.name: unit name
operands.unit_or_currency: the delivered or configured name of the Unit of Measure
operands.source: the Unit of Measure record
operands.constraints: printed only to a reader who holds the multiple-units group

operands.name: product name
operands.unit_or_currency: the display name of the product
operands.source: the product record

operands.name: the reader's group membership
operands.unit_or_currency: true or false, no unit
operands.source: the access rights of the reader
operands.constraints: decides whether the unit name is rendered

preconditions.condition: The contents are grouped by unit and product before rendering.
preconditions.otherwise: The same product in two units would print as one line with an ambiguous quantity.

procedure: Group the contents of the package by unit and product.
For each group, print the quantity, without a decimal part when it is a whole number.

operands.source: the counter sale being turned into a stock transfer

operands.unit_or_currency: two Units of Measure per move
operands.source: the move and the product
operands.constraints: the check applies to every move whose unit differs from the product's own unit

preconditions.otherwise: No conversion is performed and no zero can arise from one.

procedure: For every move whose unit differs from the product's own unit, convert the demand into the product's own unit half away from zero.
If any such conversion yields zero, refuse the whole transfer before any quantity is written.
Show the user a message that begins by stating that a conversion error occurred and that the following unit of measure conversions result in a zero quantity due to rounding.

Append one line per offending pair, each beginning with a space, a hyphen-minus, a space, then the word `From`, the source unit's name in double quotation marks, the word `to`, and the destination unit's name in double quotation marks.

Close with a paragraph explaining that the issue occurs because the quantity becomes zero after rounding during the conversion, and that to fix it the conversion factors or the rounding method must be adjusted so that even the smallest quantity in the original unit does not round down to zero in the target unit.
records.formula: quantity_in_product_unit = round_half_away_from_zero( demand × absolute_quantity( move_unit ) ÷ absolute_quantity( product_own_unit ) ) ; the transfer is refused when any such quantity_in_product_unit = 0

rounding.precision: One hundredth, the `Product Unit` step at the shipped two digits.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, which is the one method that can turn a non-zero quantity into zero at this boundary.
rounding.step: Once per move, before any quantity is written; the refusal happens before the first write.

records.name: The conditions under which a conversion rounds to zero
records.purpose: States exactly when a non-zero quantity disappears in a conversion, which is the pathology that costs a rebuild the most if it chooses the wrong rounding method at a boundary.

operands.name: exact converted value
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the destination unit, before rounding
operands.source: the quantity multiplied by the source absolute quantity and divided by the destination absolute quantity

operands.name: step
operands.unit_or_currency: a fraction of one unit
operands.source: the `Product Unit` precision

preconditions.condition: The quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The zero short-circuit of the conversion returns zero without any rounding.

procedure: Compute the exact converted value.
Under half away from zero, the result is zero when the exact value is smaller than half a step.
Under towards zero, the result is zero when the exact value is smaller than a full step.
Under away from zero, the result is never zero: any positive value, however small, is lifted to one step.
records.formula: result = 0 under half away from zero when | exact_value | < step ÷ 2 ; result = 0 under towards zero when | exact_value | < step ; result ≠ 0 under away from zero for any exact_value ≠ 0

rounding.precision: One hundredth, the `Product Unit` step at the shipped two digits.
rounding.method: All three are compared, because they disagree precisely here.
rounding.step: Once, at the end of the conversion.

result.name: the converted quantity, possibly zero
result.stored_or_displayed: returned to the calling boundary

edge_cases.case: A boundary that uses away from zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Safe against silent loss and unsafe against silent inflation.

edge_cases.case: A boundary that uses half away from zero.

operands.name: absolute quantity of the product's own unit and of the line unit
operands.unit_or_currency: counts of root units, no unit of their own
operands.source: the stored `factor` fields

preconditions.condition: The quantity is scaled up into the product's own unit while the price is scaled down to a price per the product's own unit.
preconditions.otherwise: The product of the two is no longer invariant and the accrual is out by the ratio of the two absolute quantities.

procedure: Take the ordered quantity less the already invoiced quantity as the quantity to invoice at the date.
Convert that quantity from the line's unit into the product's own unit, with the default away-from-zero rounding.
Take the line price, apply the discount, reduce it to its tax-exclusive value per one, and scale it by the ratio of the product's own absolute quantity to the line unit's absolute quantity.
Multiply the converted quantity by the gross price per the product's own unit.
records.formula: quantity_to_invoice_at_date = ordered_quantity − already_invoiced_quantity ; quantity_in_product_unit = convert_quantity( quantity_to_invoice_at_date , line_unit → product_own_unit ) ; gross_price_per_product_unit = line_price × ( 1 − discount_percentage ÷ 100 ) , then reduced to its tax-exclusive value per one , then × absolute_quantity( product_own_unit ) ÷ absolute_quantity( line_unit ) ; amount_to_invoice_at_date = quantity_in_product_unit × gross_price_per_product_unit

rounding.what: The converted quantity only; the price is never rounded by this domain.
rounding.precision: One hundredth of the product's own unit, the `Product Unit` step at the shipped two digits.
rounding.method: Away from zero on the quantity.
rounding.step: The quantity is rounded before the multiplication; the residual is at most one hundredth of the product's own unit multiplied by the price per that unit.

result.unit_or_currency: an amount in the order's currency
result.stored_or_displayed: reported by the accrual and posted by the reporting domain

edge_cases.case: The line's unit is the product's own unit.
edge_cases.outcome: Both scalings are identities and the amount is the plain quantity multiplied by the price.

edge_cases.case: An awkward quantity such as two and a half boxes.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion lands on the grid and the amount is exact.

edge_cases.case: A fractional quantity such as nought point three three boxes.
edge_cases.outcome: Forty-seven and fifty-two hundredths items lies on the grid, so the conversion introduces no error.

records.name: The accrual amount at a date when the purchase method bills the received quantity
records.purpose: The variant of the accrual computation that applies when the purchase method bills what was received rather than what was ordered; every other step is identical.

operands.name: received quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the purchase line's unit
operands.source: the purchase order line, reported from the completed receipt moves away from zero

operands.name: already invoiced quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the purchase line's unit
operands.source: the purchase order line

operands.name: line price, discount percentage and taxes
operands.unit_or_currency: an amount in the order's currency per one line unit, a percentage, and the tax set of the line
operands.source: the purchase order line

preconditions.condition: The purchase method bills the received quantity.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordered-quantity variant applies.

preconditions.condition: The received quantity has itself been converted from the move's unit into the line's unit away from zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The accrual is based on a quantity that does not match the receipt.

procedure: Take the received quantity less the already invoiced quantity as the quantity to invoice at the date.
Convert that quantity from the line's unit into the product's own unit, with the default away-from-zero rounding.
Compute the gross price per the product's own unit exactly as in the ordered-quantity variant.
Multiply the converted quantity by that price.
records.formula: quantity_to_invoice_at_date = received_quantity − already_invoiced_quantity ; quantity_in_product_unit = convert_quantity( quantity_to_invoice_at_date , line_unit → product_own_unit ) ; amount_to_invoice_at_date = quantity_in_product_unit × gross_price_per_product_unit

rounding.what: The converted quantity only, and, upstream, the received quantity itself.
rounding.precision: One hundredth, the `Product Unit` step at the shipped two digits.
rounding.method: Away from zero at both crossings.
rounding.step: The received quantity is rounded when it is reported onto the line; the accrual quantity is rounded again when it is converted into the product's own unit.

result.name: amount to invoice at the date
result.unit_or_currency: an amount in the order's currency
result.stored_or_displayed: reported by the accrual and posted by the reporting domain

edge_cases.case: Nothing has been received.
edge_cases.outcome: The quantity to invoice is zero and the accrual is nothing.

edge_cases.case: More has been received than ordered.
edge_cases.outcome: The accrual follows the receipt, because this variant bills what arrived.

edge_cases.case: Two away-from-zero roundings in sequence.
edge_cases.outcome: The accrual can exceed the exact amount by up to two hundredths of the product's own unit multiplied by the price per that unit.

worked_examples.narrative: Two boxes at the discounted box price of one hundred fourteen is two hundred twenty-eight, and the third box accrues nothing until it arrives.

records.name: The audit of a suspected unit-related ledger error
records.purpose: Reduces a journal item and its originating document line to physical quantities and prices per root unit, so that a missing or duplicated conversion can be identified from the numbers alone.

operands.name: quantity and unit of the journal item
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the unit carried by the journal item
operands.source: the posted journal item

operands.name: quantity and unit of the originating document line
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity in the line's unit
operands.source: the document line the journal item derives from

operands.name: posted amount
operands.unit_or_currency: an amount in the entry's currency
operands.source: the posted journal item

operands.name: catalogue or vendor price and the unit it is quoted in
operands.unit_or_currency: an amount per one quoted unit
operands.source: the catalogue or the vendor price list

preconditions.condition: Both sides are reduced to the root unit of the tree before being compared.
preconditions.otherwise: Two quantities in different units cannot be compared at all.

procedure: Take the journal item and note its quantity and unit.
Multiply by the unit's absolute quantity to obtain the physical quantity in root units.
Take the originating document line and do the same.

If the two physical quantities differ by more than one step of the `Product Unit` precision multiplied by the absolute quantity of the coarser unit, a conversion was applied where none was due, or omitted where one was due.
Take the posted amount and divide by the physical quantity to obtain a price per root unit.

Compare with the catalogue or vendor price divided by the absolute quantity of the unit it is quoted in; a discrepancy that is exactly a ratio of two absolute quantities identifies the missing or duplicated price conversion.
records.formula: physical_quantity = quantity × absolute_quantity( unit ) ; tolerance = step × absolute_quantity( coarser unit ) ; price_per_root_unit = posted_amount ÷ physical_quantity ; expected_price_per_root_unit = quoted_price ÷ absolute_quantity( quoted unit )

rounding.what: Nothing; the audit compares unrounded physical quantities against a stated tolerance.
rounding.precision: The tolerance is one step of the `Product Unit` precision multiplied by the absolute quantity of the coarser unit.
rounding.method: None.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the identified conversion error, or none
result.unit_or_currency: a ratio of two absolute quantities, no unit
result.stored_or_displayed: a finding; nothing is written

edge_cases.case: The two physical quantities agree within the tolerance.
edge_cases.outcome: The quantity side is sound and the price side must be examined.

edge_cases.case: The price ratio is exactly the absolute quantity of the line's unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The price conversion was omitted.

edge_cases.case: The price ratio is the reciprocal of that absolute quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The price conversion was applied twice.

worked_examples.description: The worked audit the document states

expected_outputs.conclusion: the price conversion from the product's own unit to the line's unit was not applied

worked_examples.narrative: The ratio of one hundred forty-four is exactly the absolute quantity of the box, which identifies the missing price conversion.

records.name: The derived absolute quantity and sequence of every delivered unit
records.purpose: The complete reference data as delivered, with the two derived columns carried to the last representable digit, so that a rebuild can load its own unit table and check it against a single list before running any conversion.

operands.name: contained quantity of each delivered unit
operands.unit_or_currency: a count of reference units in one of the unit, no unit of its own
operands.source: the `relative_factor` of each delivered Unit of Measure
operands.constraints: not zero; exactly one on a root unit

operands.name: reference unit of each delivered unit
operands.unit_or_currency: one Unit of Measure, or none for a root
operands.source: the `relative_uom_id` of each delivered Unit of Measure
operands.constraints: a unit of the same tree, higher in the chain

operands.name: digits of the `Product Unit` decimal precision record
operands.unit_or_currency: a count of decimal digits, no unit
operands.source: the decimal precision record
operands.constraints: two as delivered, which is what the rounding precision column reports

preconditions.condition: Each absolute quantity is computed from the stored absolute quantity of the reference unit, from the root downwards.
preconditions.otherwise: The imperial chains of the length, mass and volume trees produce different last digits.

preconditions.condition: Each sequence is derived only when the record is new or its sequence is zero.
preconditions.otherwise: A user-chosen ordering would be overwritten.

procedure: For each root unit, set the absolute quantity to the contained quantity, which validation forces to be one.
For each other unit, multiply its contained quantity by the stored absolute quantity of its reference unit.
Derive each sequence as the smaller of one thousand and the contained quantity multiplied by one hundred, truncated towards zero.
Report the rounding precision of every unit as ten raised to minus the digits of the `Product Unit` decimal precision record, which is one hundredth as delivered.
Note which units are delivered archived; an archived unit still converts and still serves the documents that reference it.
records.formula: absolute_quantity(unit) = contained_quantity(unit) × absolute_quantity( reference_unit(unit) ) , and contained_quantity(unit) for a root ; sequence = minimum( 1000 , truncate_towards_zero( contained_quantity × 100 ) ) ; rounding_precision = 10 ^ ( − 2 ) = 0.01

rounding.what: Nothing in the absolute quantity, which is stored exactly as the multiplication order produces it; the sequence is truncated.
rounding.precision: A whole number for the sequence; the rounding precision column is one hundredth for every unit.
rounding.method: Truncation towards zero for the sequence; none for the absolute quantity.
rounding.step: The sequence is truncated before the cap of one thousand is applied.

result.name: the delivered unit table with its derived columns
result.unit_or_currency: counts of root units for the absolute quantity, ordering positions for the sequence, a fraction of one unit for the rounding precision
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on each Unit of Measure as `factor`, `sequence` and `rounding`

edge_cases.case: Seven trees exist as delivered.
edge_cases.outcome: Counting, working time, length, surface, volume, mass and energy; the smallest are surface with two units and energy with one, and no conversion is possible between trees.

edge_cases.case: Units delivered archived.
edge_cases.outcome: The dozen, the centimetre, the kilometre, the inch, the foot, the yard, the mile, the square foot, the cubic metre, the United States fluid ounce, the United States quart, the United States gallon, the cubic inch, the cubic foot, the ounce and the pound are delivered archived; archiving does not affect the arithmetic.

edge_cases.case: Three absolute quantities carry visible representation error.
edge_cases.outcome: The foot, the yard and the mile, because each is derived from the stored value of the unit above rather than from an exact definition.

edge_cases.case: The minute.
edge_cases.outcome: Its contained quantity is one sixtieth rounded up at the seventh decimal digit, so an hour is fifty-nine and nine hundred ninety-nine thousandths minutes before rounding.
